01.r: Silver used as money, his to lend.
01.n: Gesenius gives the first sense as silver, so called from its pale colour; our English keeps 'silver' throughout. The Hebrew puts it first, as YLT does: 'His silver he hath not given'.

03.r: To hand over silver as a loan.
03.n: The verb is perfect, 'he has not given'; it describes a settled character, so most translations make it present, 'he that putteth not out'. The brief's lexicon includes 'lend' among the verb's uses.

04.n: The same phrase as in Leviticus 25:37 on this page, 'for interest'. Gesenius cites this verse for the noun: interest, usury.

05.r: A payment to sway a judgment against someone who has done no wrong.
05.n: Gesenius: a present, a gift, especially one to free from punishment or to corrupt a judge, and he cites this verse for 'to take a reward'. The KJV's 'reward' carries that older sense.

07.r: A man free of the charge, who would be wronged by the bribe.
07.n: Gesenius: pure, and so innocent, free from blame. The Hebrew has no 'the': 'against one who is innocent'.

09.n: Perfect, like 'given' before it. The BSB turns 'he has not taken' into 'refuses'.

10.r: Anyone whose life shows these marks.
10.n: A participle used as a noun, 'a doer of'. It closes the whole psalm, not only this verse.

11.r: The marks of the upright listed in the psalm.

12.r: With 'for ever' at the end, it means 'never'.

13.r: He will stand firm, not be overthrown.
13.n: Gesenius gives TO TOTTER, TO SHAKE, used of mountains, of a land or kingdom, and of individual persons; this form is passive, 'be shaken'.

14.n: Literally 'he shall not be shaken for ever'; Hebrew 'not ... for ever' means 'never', and English 'not ... for ever' would mislead. Gesenius gives the root sense of the noun as hidden time, a time whose end is not defined. YLT keeps 'to the age'.

01.n: Swete numbers this Psalm 14, following the Greek numbering of the psalms.

04.n: ἐπὶ τόκῳ, 'for interest'; τόκος also means offspring.

05.n: δῶρον, a gift, here plural: the Greek uses the plain word for a gift.

07.n: ἀθῷος, guiltless, plural in the Greek: 'against the innocent ones'.

11.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. ταῦτα, 'these things'.

14.n: εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, 'to the age', as YLT renders the Hebrew.
